questions.question: Which of the following quantities determines the magnitude of the buoyant force on a body?

options.text: Density of the fluid and volume displaced

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Density of the fluid and volume displaced**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Archimedes' Principle** states that when a body is immersed fully or partially in a **fluid**, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the **weight of the fluid displaced** by it.
 
• The magnitude of the **buoyant force** (also known as **upthrust**) is determined by the formula: **F = ρ × V × g**, where **ρ (rho)** is the **density of the fluid**, **V** is the **volume of the displaced fluid**, and **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• The **surface area of the body** does not affect the magnitude of the **buoyant force** directly; only the **submerged volume** matters. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **weight of the body** determines whether the object will **sink or float** when compared to the **buoyant force**, but it does not determine the magnitude of the **buoyant force** itself. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **density of the fluid and the volume of the displaced fluid** are the primary physical quantities that define how much upward force is exerted. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• The **temperature of the fluid** can indirectly affect buoyancy by changing the **fluid's density**, but it is not a direct variable in the primary **buoyancy equation**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Buoyancy** is the tendency of a **fluid** to exert an upward force on an object placed in it. This phenomenon is why objects feel lighter when submerged in **water**.
 
• **Factors affecting Buoyant Force:**
 
 
• **Volume of the object submerged:** As the **volume** of the solid submerged in the **liquid** increases, the **buoyant force** increases. Once the object is **completely immersed**, the force remains constant.
 
• **Density of the liquid:** A **liquid** with a **higher density** exerts more **buoyant force** than a **liquid** with a **lower density**. For example, it is easier to float in **seawater** (higher **density**) than in **freshwater**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Buoyancy:**
 
 
• **Ships and Submarines:** Large **ships** are designed with hollow hulls to displace a massive **volume of water**, generating enough **buoyant force** to counteract their **weight**.
 
• **Hot Air Balloons:** The **density** of the **hot air** inside the balloon is less than the **density** of the surrounding **cool air**, creating an upward **buoyant force** that allows it to rise.
 
• **Hydrometers:** These are instruments used to measure the **density** or **specific gravity** of **liquids** based on the concept of **buoyancy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conditions for Floating and Sinking:**
 
 
• If the **Buoyant Force** is greater than the **Weight** of the object, the object will **rise and float**.
 
• If the **Buoyant Force** is equal to the **Weight** of the object, the object remains **suspended** in the **fluid**.
 
• If the **Buoyant Force** is less than the **Weight** of the object, the object will **sink**.
 
 
 
• **Apparent Weight:** When an object is in a **fluid**, its **weight** appears to be less than its **actual weight** in **air**. This is because the **buoyant force** acts in the opposite direction to **gravity**. **Apparent Weight = Actual Weight - Buoyant Force**.
 
• The concept of **buoyancy** was discovered by **Archimedes** of **Syracuse** in the **3rd century BC**.

questions.question: The SI unit of average speed is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average speed** is defined as the **total distance** traveled by an object divided by the **total time elapsed** to cover that distance.
 
• In the **International System of Units (SI)**, the standard unit for **length (distance)** is the **meter (m)** and the standard unit for **time** is the **second (s)**.
 
• Since speed is the ratio of distance to time, its **derived SI unit** is **meters per second**, mathematically expressed as **m/s** or **ms⁻¹**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The unit **km/hr** (kilometers per hour) is a **practical unit** often used in vehicles and daily transport, but it is not the standard SI unit. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect in the context of SI units.***
 
• The unit **m/s²** represents **acceleration**, which measures the rate of change of velocity over time. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The unit **cm/s** (centimeters per second) belongs to the **CGS (Centimeter-Gram-Second)** system of units, not the SI system. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** **Average speed** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it only has **magnitude** and no specific direction. Unlike **velocity**, it does not account for the displacement or the path's direction.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for speed is **[M⁰ L¹ T⁻¹]**. This indicates that speed depends on **length (L)** and **inverse time (T)**, with no dependence on **mass (M)**.
 
• **Unit Conversion:** It is frequently necessary to convert between different units of speed. To convert from **km/hr** to **m/s**, we multiply by a factor of **5/18** (since 1000m / 3600s = 5/18). Conversely, to convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, we multiply by **18/5**.
 
• **Instantaneous Speed vs. Average Speed:** While average speed looks at the entire journey, **instantaneous speed** refers to the speed of an object at a **specific moment in time**, often measured by a **speedometer** in a car.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distance vs. Displacement:** It is important to distinguish between speed and **velocity**. Average speed uses **total distance**, whereas **average velocity** is calculated using **total displacement** divided by total time.
 
• **Uniform Motion:** If an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in **uniform motion**, and its instantaneous speed will be equal to its average speed throughout the journey.
 
• **Mathematical Expression:** The formula for average speed is written as: **v = Δd / Δt**, where **v** is the average speed, **Δd** is the total distance, and **Δt** is the total time taken.

questions.question: If the distance-time graph of an object is a straight line parallel to the time axis, what is the object's speed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **distance-time graph** is a graphical representation used in physics to show how the **distance** traveled by an object changes with respect to **time**. The **time** is usually plotted on the **X-axis** and the **distance** is plotted on the **Y-axis**.
 
• When the distance-time graph is a **straight line parallel to the time axis**, it implies that the **distance** value on the Y-axis does not change even as **time** (on the X-axis) continues to increase.
 
• The **slope** of a distance-time graph represents the **speed** of the object. Mathematically, the **slope** is calculated as the change in **distance** divided by the change in **time** (**Speed = Δd / Δt**).
 
• In the case of a horizontal line, the **change in distance (Δd)** is **0**. Therefore, the **speed** of the object is **0 divided by the change in time**, which results in a **speed** of **Zero**.
 
• This state indicates that the object is **stationary** or **at rest**. It is located at a specific **position** away from the **origin**, but its position does not shift over **time**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Zero.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Speed:**
 
 
• If the distance-time graph is a **straight line** passing through the **origin** with a specific **inclination (slope)**, it represents **Uniform Speed**.
 
• In this scenario, the object covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**. The **speed** remains **constant** and **non-zero** throughout the **motion**.
 
 
 
• **Non-Uniform Speed (Acceleration):**
 
 
• If the distance-time graph is a **curve** (such as a **parabola**), it represents **non-uniform motion**.
 
• A curve indicates that the **speed** of the object is changing at every point in **time**, meaning the object is either **accelerating** or **decelerating**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Velocity-Time Graph:**
 
 
• It is crucial to distinguish between different types of **motion graphs**. In a **velocity-time graph**, a **straight line parallel to the time axis** represents **constant velocity** (where **acceleration** is **zero**), not zero speed.
 
• However, in a **distance-time graph**, that same horizontal line strictly means the object is **not moving**.
 
 
 
• **Physical Significance of the Origin:**
 
 
• The **origin (0,0)** typically represents the **starting point** or the **reference point** from which **measurement** begins.
 
• If the horizontal line is exactly on the **time axis** (where **distance = 0**), the object is **at rest** at the **reference point** itself. If the line is above the axis, the object is **at rest** at a certain **fixed distance** from the **reference point**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scalar vs Vector:** **Distance** is a **scalar quantity**, and **speed** is the **magnitude** of **velocity**. Because **distance** can never decrease over **time**, a distance-time graph can never have a **negative slope** (it cannot go downwards).
 
• **Slope Analysis:** The steeper the **slope** of the line in a distance-time graph, the higher the **speed** of the object. A **vertical line** (parallel to the distance axis) is **physically impossible**, as it would imply **infinite speed** (covering distance in zero time).
 
• **Calculation:** To find the **speed** from a linear graph, pick two points **(t1, d1)** and **(t2, d2)** and use the formula **v = (d2 - d1) / (t2 - t1)**. For a horizontal line, **d2** always equals **d1**, making the numerator **zero**.

questions.question: Which of the following salts will have a pH close to 7 when dissolved in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NaCl**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** is a **neutral salt** formed by the **neutralization reaction** between a **strong acid** and a **strong base**.
 
• It is synthesized from **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, which is a **strong acid**, and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, which is a **strong base**.
 
• When **NaCl** is dissolved in **water**, it dissociates completely into its constituent ions, **Na+** and **Cl-**. Neither of these ions reacts significantly with water (hydrolysis) to produce excess **H+** or **OH-** ions.
 
• Because there is no significant hydrolysis, the concentration of **hydrogen ions** and **hydroxide ions** remains balanced, resulting in a **pH of approximately 7** at **25 degrees Celsius**. ***Hence, the statement regarding NaCl is correct.***
 
• The **pH scale** measures the acidity or alkalinity of a solution, where **7** is considered **neutral**, values below **7** are **acidic**, and values above **7** are **basic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3):**
 
 
• This salt is formed from a **strong base (NaOH)** and a **weak acid (H2CO3 - Carbonic acid)**.
 
• In an aqueous solution, the **carbonate ion (CO3 2-)** undergoes hydrolysis to produce **hydroxide ions (OH-)**.
 
• Consequently, the solution becomes **basic**, and the **pH is greater than 7**. ***Hence, the option Na2CO3 is incorrect for a pH of 7.***
 
 
 
• **Sodium Acetate (CH3COONa):**
 
 
• It is the product of a **strong base (NaOH)** and a **weak acid (CH3COOH - Acetic acid)**.
 
• The **acetate ion (CH3COO-)** reacts with water to form **acetic acid** and **hydroxide ions**.
 
• This increases the **OH-** concentration, making the solution **alkaline** with a **pH typically around 8.9**. ***Hence, the option CH3COONa is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Ammonium Chloride (NH4Cl):**
 
 
• This salt is formed from a **weak base (NH4OH - Ammonium hydroxide)** and a **strong acid (HCl)**.
 
• The **ammonium ion (NH4+)** undergoes hydrolysis in water, releasing **H+ ions** into the solution.
 
• This makes the resulting solution **acidic**, with a **pH usually between 4.5 and 6.0**. ***Hence, the option NH4Cl is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Salt Hydrolysis:** This is a chemical reaction in which the **cations** or **anions** of a salt react with **water** to affect the **pH** of the solution.
 
• **Strong Electrolytes:** Salts like **NaCl** are **strong electrolytes** that ionize completely in **water**.
 
• **Predicting pH:**
 
 
• **Strong Acid + Strong Base = Neutral Solution (pH = 7)**.
 
• **Strong Acid + Weak Base = Acidic Solution (pH 7)**.
 
• **Weak Acid + Weak Base = pH depends on the relative strengths of the acid and base**.
 
 
 
• **Year and Context:** The understanding of **acids and bases** was significantly advanced by the **Arrhenius theory** in the **late 19th century** and later by the **Bronsted-Lowry** and **Lewis** definitions in the **early 20th century** (around **1923**).
</ul

questions.question: Copper reacts with moist carbon dioxide in the air and slowly loses its shiny brown surface and gains a _________ colour coating of basic copper carbonate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**green**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Copper** is a **lustrous, reddish-brown metal** that reacts slowly with the environment when exposed to **moist air** for a prolonged period.
 
• The metal reacts with **moist carbon dioxide** and **oxygen** present in the atmosphere, leading to the formation of a **green-colored** layer on its surface.
 
• This **green coating** is chemically known as **basic copper carbonate**, which is a mixture of **copper carbonate (CuCO3)** and **copper hydroxide (Cu(OH)2)**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the green color is correct.***
 
• The chemical reaction can be represented as: **2Cu + H2O + CO2 + O2 → Cu(OH)2 + CuCO3**.
 
• The formation of this layer is a classic example of **corrosion**, where the metal loses its **shiny brown surface** and develops a dull finish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Corrosion of Silver:**
 
 
• **Silver** articles become **black** after some time when exposed to air.
 
• This happens because silver reacts with **sulphur** (often in the form of hydrogen sulphide) in the air to form a coating of **silver sulphide (Ag2S)**.
 
 
 
• **Corrosion of Iron (Rusting):**
 
 
• When **iron** is exposed to **moist air** for a long time, it acquires a coating of a **brown flaky substance** called **rust**.
 
• Chemically, rust is **hydrated ferric oxide (Fe2O3.xH2O)**. Unlike the green coating on copper, rust is porous and causes the metal to deteriorate continuously.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Copper:**
 
 
• **Copper** is an excellent conductor of **heat and electricity**, making it essential for **electrical wiring** and **cookware**.
 
• It is highly **malleable and ductile**, allowing it to be drawn into thin wires or beaten into sheets.
 
• The **statue of liberty** in the **USA** is a famous example of copper corrosion; it was originally **brown** but turned **green** over decades due to the formation of **basic copper carbonate** and other salts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prevention of Corrosion:**
 
 
• Corrosion can be prevented by methods such as **painting**, **oiling**, **greasing**, or **galvanizing**.
 
• **Galvanization** is a method of protecting **steel and iron** from rusting by coating them with a thin layer of **zinc**.
 
• **Alloying** is another very good method of improving the properties of a metal. For example, **brass** is an alloy of **copper and zinc**, while **bronze** is an alloy of **copper and tin**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Nature:**
 
 
• The **green patina** formed on copper is **basic** in nature. It can often be cleaned using **weak acids** like **citric acid** (found in **lemon** or **tamarind**), which dissolves the **basic copper carbonate**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In electrolytic refining, the impure metal is used as the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**anode**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrolytic refining** is one of the most widely used techniques for the purification of **impure metals** such as **Copper**, **Zinc**, **Tin**, **Nickel**, **Silver**, and **Gold**.
 
• In this process, a thick block of the **impure metal** is used as the **anode**, which is the **positively charged electrode**. ***Hence, the correct answer is anode.***
 
• A thin strip of **pure metal** is used as the **cathode**, which is the **negatively charged electrode**.
 
• The **electrolyte** used in the process is a **water-soluble salt** (aqueous solution) of the same metal that is being refined, often acidified to increase conductivity.
 
• When an **electric current** is passed through the electrolyte, the **impure metal** from the **anode** dissolves into the **electrolyte** solution in the form of **metal ions**.
 
• Simultaneously, an equivalent amount of **pure metal** from the electrolyte is deposited onto the **cathode**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Refining:**
 
 
• At the **anode**, **oxidation** takes place. The metal atoms lose electrons to become ions: **M → Mⁿ⁺ + ne−**.
 
• At the **cathode**, **reduction** takes place. The metal ions gain electrons to become pure metal atoms: **Mⁿ⁺ + ne− → M**.
 
 
 
• **Anode Mud:**
 
 
• During the process, **soluble impurities** go into the solution, whereas **insoluble impurities** settle down at the bottom of the **anode**.
 
• These collected impurities are known as **anode mud**. In the case of **Copper** refining, the anode mud often contains valuable metals like **Antimony**, **Selenium**, **Tellurium**, **Silver**, **Gold**, and **Platinum**, which helps recover the cost of the refining process.
 
 
 
• **Example - Copper Refining:**
 
 
• To refine **Copper (Cu)**, the **anode** is made of **blister copper** (impure).
 
• The **cathode** is a thin sheet of **pure copper**.
 
• The **electrolyte** is a solution of **Copper Sulphate (CuSO₄)** acidified with **Sulphuric Acid (H₂SO₄)**.
 
• This method can achieve a purity level of **99.95%** to **99.99%**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Electrolyte:**
 
 
• The **electrolyte** acts as a medium for the transfer of metal ions from the **positive electrode** to the **negative electrode**.
 
• The concentration of the metal ions in the **electrolyte** remains constant throughout the process because the rate of dissolution at the **anode** equals the rate of deposition at the **cathode**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Voltage Control:** The **voltage** applied during **electrolytic refining** is carefully controlled to ensure that only the desired metal is deposited at the **cathode**, leaving other **metallic impurities** either in the solution or as **anode mud**.
 
• **Electro-winning vs. Electrolytic Refining:** While **electrolytic refining** purifies a metal from an impure block, **electro-winning** involves the extraction of metals from their ores or compounds already dissolved in an electrolyte.
 
• **Industrial Use:** This process is critical in the **electronics industry**, where high-conductivity **pure copper** is required for wiring and **integrated circuits**.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the division of labour seen in multicellular organisms?

options.text: Each body part is made up of a single cell
Multicellular organisms have only one type of cell
All cells perform the same function in an organism

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Different cells have specialized functions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Multicellular organisms** are composed of more than one cell, often numbering in the **millions or billions**. These organisms range from simple forms like **fungi** and **algae** to complex forms like **plants** and **animals**.
 
• The concept of **division of labour** in these organisms refers to the delegation of specific biological tasks to different groups of cells. This means that instead of a single cell performing all life processes, different cells are **specialized** to carry out specific roles. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• In **multicellular organisms**, body parts are not made of a single cell but of vast clusters of cells working together. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• These organisms possess a wide variety of cell types, such as **nerve cells**, **muscle cells**, and **blood cells**, rather than just one type. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Cells in a complex organism do not perform the same function; for instance, a **muscle cell** is designed for contraction and movement, while a **neuron** is designed to transmit electrical impulses. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **division of labour** leads to increased efficiency, allowing the organism to perform complex survival activities simultaneously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Levels of Biological Organization:**
 
 
• **Cells:** The basic structural and functional unit of life. In **multicellular** beings, cells undergo **differentiation** to become specialized.
 
• **Tissues:** A group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function. Examples include **connective tissue**, **epithelial tissue**, and **vascular tissue** in plants.
 
• **Organs:** Different types of tissues group together to form an organ, such as the **heart**, **lungs**, or **stomach**, to conduct specific physiological tasks.
 
• **Organ Systems:** Multiple organs coordinate to form a system, like the **digestive system** or the **respiratory system**.
 
 
 
• **Specialization Examples in Humans:**
 
 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs):** Specialized to transport **oxygen** throughout the body using **hemoglobin**.
 
• **White Blood Cells (WBCs):** Part of the **immune system**, specialized to fight infections and foreign pathogens.
 
• **Nerve Cells:** Long and branched cells specialized for the rapid conduction of **nerve impulses**.
 
 
 
• **Specialization in Plants:**
 
 
• **Xylem:** Specialized tissue for the conduction of **water and minerals** from roots to leaves.
 
• **Phloem:** Specialized for the translocation of **food (sucrose)** from leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• **Guard Cells:** Specialized cells in the **epidermis** of leaves that control the opening and closing of **stomata** for gas exchange.

questions.question: How is the change in Gravitational Potential Energy ( Delta PE_g ) of a system related to the work ( W_g ) done by the gravitational force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wg = -ΔPEg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between work and energy is fundamental in **Classical Mechanics**. For any **conservative force**, the **work done** (**W**) by the force is defined as the **negative change** in the **potential energy** (**ΔPE**) of the system.
 
• When an object is moved against the **gravitational force** (e.g., lifting it **upward**), the **displacement** is opposite to the direction of **gravity**. In this case, **gravity** does **negative work**, while the **Gravitational Potential Energy** of the system **increases**. *Hence, option 2 is correct.*
 
• Mathematically, if an object of **mass (m)** is moved from a **height (h₁)** to **(h₂)**, the change in potential energy is **ΔPEg = mgh₂ - mgh₁**. The work done by gravity during this displacement is **Wg = -mg(h₂ - h₁)**.
 
• If **gravity** does **positive work** (e.g., an object falling **downward**), the **displacement** and **force** are in the same direction, which results in a **decrease** in the system's **potential energy**.
 
• This relationship ensures that the **Total Mechanical Energy** of an isolated system remains **constant** when only **conservative forces** are acting. *Hence, option 4 is incorrect as it neglects the sign convention.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Conservative Forces:**
 
 
• A force is **conservative** if the **work done** by it in moving an object between two points is **independent of the path** taken.
 
• Examples include **Gravitational force**, **Electrostatic force**, and **Spring force**. For these forces, we can always define a **Potential Energy** function.
 
• In contrast, **non-conservative forces** like **friction** or **air resistance** depend on the path taken, and the energy is dissipated as **heat**.
 
 
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:**
 
 
• This theorem states that the **net work done** by all forces (both conservative and non-conservative) on an object is equal to the change in its **Kinetic Energy (ΔKE)**.
 
• In a vacuum where only **gravity** acts, **Wg = ΔKE**. Since **Wg = -ΔPEg**, it follows that **ΔKE = -ΔPEg**, or **ΔKE + ΔPEg = 0**, representing the **conservation of energy**.
 
 
 
• **SI Units and Scalar Nature:**
 
 
• Both **Work** and **Potential Energy** are **scalar quantities**, meaning they have magnitude but no specific spatial direction, though they can have **positive or negative values**.
 
• The **SI unit** for both is the **Joule (J)**, named after the **English physicist James Prescott Joule**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reference Level:** The value of **Potential Energy** depends on the **reference point** (datum) chosen. Usually, the **surface of the Earth** is assigned a **PE** of **zero**. However, the **change (ΔPE)** remains the same regardless of the reference level.
 
• **Gravity Constant:** Near the **Earth's surface**, the **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. This value was famously studied by **Galileo Galilei** in the **16th century**.
 
• **Universal Gravitation:** For objects far from Earth, the potential energy formula changes to **U = -GmM/r**, where **G** is the **Gravitational Constant** (**6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg²**), as formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**.
 
• **Sign Significance:** The **negative sign** in **Wg = -ΔPEg** is not just a mathematical artifact; it signifies that **work** is done **against** the field to store energy within it.

questions.question: A compound is a substance in which elements are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemically combined in fixed proportion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more chemical **elements** are **chemically bonded** together in a **fixed proportion** by **mass**.
 
• The constituent elements in a compound lose their individual properties. For example, **Water (H2O)** is a liquid used to extinguish fires, even though it is composed of **Hydrogen** (a highly combustible gas) and **Oxygen** (a supporter of combustion).
 
• Elements in a compound are not **easily separable** by **physical methods** like filtration or handpicking because they are held together by strong **chemical bonds**. Separation requires **chemical** or **electrochemical reactions**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **mixture** consists of substances **physically mixed in any ratio**, whereas a compound must have a **specific, constant ratio** of its components. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The bonding in a compound is permanent and stable under standard conditions, not **mixed temporarily**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **fixed proportion** is a fundamental characteristic defined by the **Law of Definite Proportions**, which states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a **fixed ratio** by **weight**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Bonding**: The atoms in a compound are joined by either **ionic bonds** (electrostatic attraction between ions) or **covalent bonds** (sharing of electrons). These bonds determine the **molecular structure** and **stability** of the substance.
 
• **Homogeneity**: Every compound is a **homogeneous substance**. This means that no matter which part of the compound is sampled, the **chemical composition** and **physical properties** remain identical throughout.
 
• **Energy Changes**: The formation of a compound from its constituent elements usually involves a significant **change in energy**. Energy is either **evolved** (exothermic) or **absorbed** (endothermic) in the form of **heat** or **light**.
 
• **Fixed Melting and Boiling Points**: Unlike mixtures, which melt or boil over a range of temperatures, pure compounds have **sharp and well-defined melting and boiling points**. This serves as a primary method for **purity testing** in laboratories.
 
• **Examples**: Common examples include **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, which always contains **Sodium** and **Chlorine** in a **1:1 atomic ratio**, and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**, which always has **1 atom of Carbon** for every **2 atoms of Oxygen**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Definite Proportions**: Proposed by the **French chemist Joseph Proust** in **1799**, this law is the cornerstone of **stoichiometry**. It implies that the **mass ratio** of elements in a compound like **Ammonia (NH3)** is always **14:3** (Nitrogen to Hydrogen), regardless of how the compound is prepared.
 
• **Physical vs Chemical Separation**: While a mixture of **Iron** and **Sulphur** can be separated using a **magnet**, the compound **Iron Sulphide (FeS)** cannot be separated by a magnet because the **Iron** has chemically reacted with the **Sulphur** to form a new substance.
 
• **Electrolysis**: Some compounds, like **Aluminium Oxide** or **Water**, require the passage of an **electric current** (a process called **electrolysis**) to break the **chemical bonds** and retrieve the original elements.
 
• **Representation**: Every compound is represented by a **chemical formula**. This formula represents the **number** and **type** of **atoms** present in the **smallest unit** (molecule or formula unit) of the substance.
</ul

questions.question: Corrosion of iron is commonly known as rusting, and it requires:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**water and atmospheric oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rusting** is a specific type of **Corrosion** that occurs specifically on the surface of **Iron** and its alloys, such as steel.
 
• For rusting to take place, two conditions are absolutely essential: the presence of **Oxygen** (usually from the **Atmosphere**) and the presence of **Water** or **Moisture**.
 
• Chemically, rusting is an **Oxidation** reaction where iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of water to form **Hydrated Iron(III) Oxide**, represented by the chemical formula **Fe2O3·nH2O**.
 
• It is considered an **Electrochemical Process** because different areas of the metal surface act as **Anodes** and **Cathodes**, where electrons flow through the metal while ions move through the water film on the surface.
 
• If iron is kept in **Vacuum** (no air) or in **Dry Air** (no moisture), it will not rust; similarly, iron submerged in **Boiled Distilled Water** (where dissolved oxygen is removed) and sealed from air will also not rust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Accelerating Rusting:**
 
 
• The rate of rusting increases significantly in the presence of **Electrolytes**. For example, **Saltwater** (common in **Coastal Areas**) speeds up the electrochemical reaction, leading to faster degradation of ships and bridges.
 
• **High Acidity** (low pH) also accelerates the process because hydrogen ions facilitate the reduction of oxygen at the cathodic sites.
 
 
 
• **Prevention Methods:**
 
 
• **Galvanization:** This is a common method where a protective layer of **Zinc** is applied to iron or steel. Zinc is more reactive and acts as a **Sacrificial Anode**, corroding itself to protect the underlying iron.
 
• **Alloying:** Mixing iron with other elements like **Chromium** and **Nickel** creates **Stainless Steel**. Chromium forms a thin, invisible layer of **Chromium Oxide** that prevents oxygen and water from reaching the iron.
 
• **Barrier Protection:** Simple methods like **Painting**, **Oiling**, or **Greasing** the surface of the metal create a physical barrier that blocks contact with **Atmospheric Oxygen** and **Moisture**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:** **Corrosion** is a major global issue, resulting in the loss of nearly **3% to 4%** of a country's **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** annually due to the replacement and maintenance of rusted infrastructure and machinery.
 
• **Chemical Equation:** The simplified reaction can be written as: **4Fe + 3O2 + 2nH2O → 2Fe2O3·nH2O**. This reddish-brown substance is flaky and porous, which allows the rusting process to continue deep into the metal until the object is completely destroyed.

questions.question: The law of conservation of mass states that:

options.text: Matter can be created in reactions
Mass always decreases during a reaction
Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
Matter can be destroyed during reactions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass** states that in an isolated or **closed system**, matter is neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction or physical transformation.
 
• According to this law, the **total mass of the reactants** participating in a chemical reaction must be exactly equal to the **total mass of the products** formed.
 
• This principle was famously established and verified by the **French chemist Antoine Lavoisier** in **1789**, marking a turning point from alchemy to **modern chemistry**.
 
• At the atomic level, the law implies that the **number of atoms** of each element remains constant; they are simply **rearranged** from one state or combination to another. ***Hence, the third option is correct.***
 
• The statement that matter can be created or destroyed during reactions is scientifically incorrect in the context of chemical processes. ***Hence, statements 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antoine Lavoisier (1743–1794):**

 
 
• Often referred to as the **Father of Modern Chemistry**, he conducted meticulous experiments such as the **combustion of phosphorus** and **sulfur** to prove that mass is conserved.
 
• He demonstrated that even though substances change their state (e.g., solid to gas), the **total weight** remains unchanged if the gases are captured.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Stoichiometry:**
 
 
• The law serves as the fundamental basis for **balancing chemical equations**.
 
• For instance, in the formation of **water (H2O)**, the mass of **Hydrogen (H2)** and **Oxygen (O2)** used must match the mass of the water produced.
 
 
 
• **Closed System vs. Open System:**
 
 
• In a **closed system**, no matter can escape, making it easy to observe mass conservation.
 
• In an **open system**, such as a burning log, mass might appear to decrease because **carbon dioxide** and **water vapor** escape into the **atmosphere**.
 
 
 
• **Related Laws of Chemical Combination:**
 
 
• **Law of Definite Proportions:** Proposed by **Joseph Proust**, stating that a chemical compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by mass.
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:** Proposed by **John Dalton**, stating that if two elements form more than one compound, the ratios of the masses of the second element that combine with a fixed mass of the first element will be **small whole numbers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass-Energy Equivalence:** In modern physics, specifically **nuclear reactions**, mass and energy can be interconverted according to **Albert Einstein’s** equation **E=mc²**. However, in standard **chemical reactions**, the energy changes are so small that the change in mass is **negligible**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Before **1789**, many scientists believed in the "**phlogiston theory**," which suggested that mass was lost during combustion because a substance called phlogiston was released. **Lavoisier's** discovery effectively **disproved** this theory.
 
• **Practical Example:** When **12 grams** of **Carbon** reacts with **32 grams** of **Oxygen**, it will always produce exactly **44 grams** of **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**, provided the reaction goes to completion.

questions.question: What is the method of removal of metabolic waste in many unicellular organisms?

options.text: Through the use of special organs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Through a simple diffusion process**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unicellular organisms**, such as **Amoeba**, **Paramecium**, and **Bacteria**, consist of a single cell that performs all vital biological functions including nutrition, respiration, and excretion.
 
• In these organisms, **metabolic wastes** (predominantly **ammonia**) are produced as by-products of cellular activities. Because they lack specialized excretory organs like **kidneys**, they rely on the physical process of **diffusion**.
 
• **Simple diffusion** is the movement of waste molecules from an area of **higher concentration** (inside the cell) to an area of **lower concentration** (the surrounding external environment) across the **semi-permeable cell membrane**.
 
• The high **surface-area-to-volume ratio** of **unicellular organisms** ensures that the entire body surface is in direct contact with the environment, making the **diffusion process** highly efficient for waste removal.
 
• Unlike complex animals that require **circulatory systems** and **specialized organs**, the **metabolic waste** in single-celled life forms is simply released into the surrounding water medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Metabolic Waste:** These are substances left over from **metabolic processes** (such as cellular respiration) which cannot be used by the organism and may be toxic if accumulated. Examples include **carbon dioxide**, **water**, and **nitrogenous compounds**.
 
• **Osmoregulation vs. Excretion:**
 
 
• While **metabolic waste** is removed via **diffusion**, many **freshwater unicellular organisms** use **contractile vacuoles** for **osmoregulation**.
 
• The **contractile vacuole** collects excess water that enters the cell through **osmosis** and pumps it out to prevent the cell from bursting.
 
 
 
• **Excretory Mechanisms in Other Organisms:**
 
 
• **Flatworms:** Use specialized cells called **flame cells** (protonephridia) for excretion.
 
• **Earthworms:** Utilize tubular structures called **nephridia**.
 
• **Insects:** Use **Malpighian tubules** to remove nitrogenous wastes.
 
• **Vertebrates:** Possess complex **kidneys** containing millions of functional units called **nephrons** to filter blood and produce urine.
 
 
 
• **Diffusion vs. Osmosis:**
 
 
• **Diffusion** refers to the movement of any substance (solute or gas) from high to low concentration.
 
• **Osmosis** is a specific type of diffusion referring only to the movement of **water molecules** through a semi-permeable membrane.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ammonotelism:** Most aquatic **unicellular organisms** are **ammonotelic**, meaning they excrete **ammonia** as their primary nitrogenous waste. **Ammonia** is highly toxic but very soluble in water, allowing it to **diffuse** quickly into the environment.
 
• **Plasma Membrane Role:** The **plasma membrane** acts as the primary interface for gas exchange and waste disposal. **Carbon dioxide** produced during respiration also leaves the cell via **simple diffusion**.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** The efficiency of **diffusion** is dependent on the concentration gradient; if the surrounding water is polluted or has high concentrations of waste, the **unicellular organism** may struggle to clear its internal metabolic by-products.
</ul

questions.question: Which statement best describes the Law of Constant Proportion of the compound water?

options.text: The properties of compounds are the same as those of elements.
A chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in a fixed ratio by mass.
Elements combine in any ratio to form compounds.
The total mass of products is always greater than reactants in a reaction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in a fixed ratio by mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Constant Proportions**, also known as the **Law of Definite Proportions**, states that in a **chemical substance**, the elements are always present in **definite proportions by mass**.
 
• This law was formulated by the **French chemist Joseph Proust** in **1799**. It implies that regardless of the **source** or the **method of preparation**, a pure chemical compound will always consist of the same **elements** combined in the same **fixed mass ratio**.
 
• In the case of **water** (chemical formula **H2O**), the elements **hydrogen** and **oxygen** are always present in a **ratio of 1:8 by mass**. This means that if **9 grams** of water is decomposed, **1 gram** of hydrogen and **8 grams** of oxygen are always obtained. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The properties of a **compound** are entirely different from the properties of its constituent **elements**. For example, hydrogen is **combustible** and oxygen supports **combustion**, but water is used to **extinguish fires**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Elements do not combine in "any" ratio to form compounds; they follow **stoichiometric laws**. A mixture might have components in any ratio, but a **chemical compound** requires a **fixed ratio**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass** states that mass is neither **created** nor **destroyed** in a chemical reaction; therefore, the **total mass of products** must be **equal** to the **total mass of reactants**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass**:
 
 
• Proposed by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1789**.
 
• It establishes that during any **physical or chemical change**, the total mass of the **matter** remains **constant**.
 
• This principle is fundamental to **balancing chemical equations** in **chemistry**.
 
 
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions**:
 
 
• Proposed by **John Dalton** in **1803**.
 
• It states that if two elements combine to form **more than one compound**, the masses of one element that combine with a **fixed mass** of the other element are in the ratio of **small whole numbers**.
 
• Example: Carbon and oxygen can form **Carbon Monoxide (CO)** and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**.
 
 
 
• **Dalton's Atomic Theory**:
 
 
• In **1808**, **John Dalton** provided an explanation for the laws of chemical combination.
 
• One of his key **postulates** was that "the **relative number and kinds of atoms** are constant in a given **compound**," which supports the Law of Constant Proportions.
 
 
 
• **Ammonia (NH3) Example**:
 
 
• In **Ammonia**, **nitrogen** and **hydrogen** are always present in the **ratio of 14:3 by mass**.
 
• This remains true whether the ammonia is produced in a **laboratory** or obtained from **atmospheric sources**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Calculation of Mass Ratio in Water**:
 
 
• The **atomic mass** of **Hydrogen** is approximately **1 unit**.
 
• The **atomic mass** of **Oxygen** is approximately **16 units**.
 
• In **H2O**, there are **2 atoms** of Hydrogen and **1 atom** of Oxygen.
 
• Mass ratio = (2 x 1) : (1 x 16) = **2 : 16**, which simplifies to **1 : 8**.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions to the Law**:
 
 
• The law does not strictly hold for **non-stoichiometric compounds** (like some metal oxides) where the ratio of elements can vary slightly.
 
• It also does not account for **isotopes**. For example, water made with **Deuterium** (Heavy Water or **D2O**) will have a different mass ratio (**2:8 or 1:4**) compared to normal water.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Significance**:
 
 
• This law allowed chemists to determine **atomic weights** and understand the **molecular structure** of substances during the **19th century**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The random wavering or flickering of objects viewed through a turbulent stream of hot air rising above a fire or radiator is an effect of ______________.

options.text: Atmospheric refraction on a small scale

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmospheric refraction on a small scale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The wavering or flickering of objects seen through hot air is primarily caused by **Atmospheric Refraction** occurring on a local or **small scale**. This happens because the air just above a **fire** or **radiator** becomes significantly hotter than the surrounding air.
 
• Hot air is **lighter** and **less dense** than the cooler air above it, and it possesses a **lower refractive index** than the cooler air. Since the physical conditions of the air are not stationary due to **convection** and **turbulence**, the refractive index of the medium is constantly **fluctuating**.
 
• When light from an object passes through these layers of air with **varying refractive indices**, the path of the light rays is bent or **refracted** multiple times in random directions.
 
• As the **optical density** of the air through which the light passes changes rapidly, the **apparent position** of the object as seen by the eye fluctuates. This creates the visual effect of **wavering** or **flickering**. ***Hence, Option 4 is the correct statement.***
 
• This phenomenon is an **optical illusion** caused by the medium (air) and not by any change in the object itself or the properties of the light source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric Refraction:** This refers to the **deviation of light** from a straight line as it passes through the atmosphere due to variations in **air density** as a function of **altitude** and **temperature**. On a large scale, it is responsible for the **twinkling of stars** and the **early sunrise** and **delayed sunset** (approximately **2 minutes** difference).
 
• **Tyndall Effect:** This is the **scattering of light** by **colloidal particles** or very fine suspended particles in a medium, such as dust or smoke in the air. While it makes a **beam of light visible**, it does not cause the wavering of distant objects. ***Hence, Option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Diffraction of Light:** This is the **bending of light** around the **edges of an obstacle** or through a small opening. It is a **wave property** of light that occurs when the obstacle size is comparable to the **wavelength** of light. It is not the cause of thermal flickering. ***Hence, Option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Heat Radiation:** Heat is transferred from a fire through **conduction, convection, and radiation (Infrared)**. While radiation carries energy, the **visual distortion** is a result of the air (the medium) through which the light travels, not the radiation process itself. ***Hence, Option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Refractive Index and Temperature:** Generally, for gases like air, the **refractive index** is inversely proportional to the **absolute temperature**. As temperature increases, density decreases, leading to a **lower refractive index**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirages:** Another famous example of **atmospheric refraction** is a **mirage**, often seen on hot **highways** or in **deserts**. This is caused by the **total internal reflection** of light at the layers of air near the ground that have different **temperature gradients**.
 
• **Optical Density:** It is a measure of the speed of light in a medium. A medium with a **higher refractive index** is called **optically denser**, and light travels **slower** in it compared to an **optically rarer** medium.
 
• **Apparent Position:** Due to refraction, objects in the sky (like the **Sun** or **Stars**) always appear slightly **higher** than their **actual position** because light bends toward the **normal** as it enters the denser layers of the **Earth's atmosphere**.
</ul

questions.question: A decrease in oxygen availability in the environment is most likely to first impact which step of aerobic respiration in animal cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electron transport chain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Electron Transport Chain (ETC)** is the final stage of **aerobic respiration** and is located in the **inner mitochondrial membrane**.
 
• Oxygen acts as the **terminal electron acceptor** in this process; it combines with electrons and **hydrogen ions** to form **water (H2O)**.
 
• A decrease in **oxygen availability** immediately halts the flow of electrons through the **protein complexes** (Complex I to IV), as there is no molecule to receive them at the end of the chain. *Hence, the statement regarding the Electron transport chain being the first impacted is correct.*
 
• Without oxygen, **oxidative phosphorylation** cannot occur, leading to a sudden drop in the production of **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**, which is the primary energy currency of the cell.
 
• The failure of the ETC leads to an accumulation of **NADH** and **FADH2**, which are normally oxidized back into **NAD+** and **FAD** to sustain other metabolic pathways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glycolysis:**
 
 
• This process occurs in the **cytoplasm** of the cell and involves the breakdown of **glucose** into two molecules of **pyruvate**.
 
• It is an **anaerobic process**, meaning it does not require oxygen to proceed. Therefore, it is not the first step impacted by a lack of oxygen. *Hence, the statement regarding Glycolysis is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Krebs Cycle (Citric Acid Cycle):**
 
 
• This cycle takes place in the **mitochondrial matrix** and produces **CO2**, **ATP**, **NADH**, and **FADH2**.
 
• While it does not use oxygen directly, it eventually stops because it requires **NAD+** and **FAD**, which are only regenerated when the ETC is functioning. However, this is a secondary impact following the ETC failure. *Hence, the statement regarding the Krebs cycle is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Lactic Acid Fermentation:**
 
 
• In animal cells (especially **skeletal muscle**), when oxygen is limited, the cell resorts to **fermentation** to regenerate **NAD+** so that glycolysis can continue.
 
• This is a **consequence** or an alternative pathway triggered by the lack of oxygen, rather than the "step of aerobic respiration" that is first negatively impacted. *Hence, the statement regarding Lactic acid fermentation is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Cellular Respiration Facts:**
 
 
• **Aerobic respiration** yields approximately **36 to 38 ATP** per glucose molecule, whereas **anaerobic respiration** (fermentation) yields only **2 ATP**.
 
• The **mitochondria** are known as the **powerhouse of the cell** because they host the Krebs Cycle and the ETC, where the majority of energy is harvested.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hypoxia** is the medical term for a condition where the body or a region of the body is deprived of adequate **oxygen supply** at the tissue level.
 
• The **Chemiosmotic theory**, proposed by **Peter Mitchell** in **1961**, explains how the ETC creates a **proton gradient** across the inner mitochondrial membrane to drive **ATP synthase**.
 
• In the absence of oxygen, the **proton motive force** dissipates, which not only stops ATP production but can also lead to the formation of **Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS)** if oxygen levels are fluctuating or partially restored (reperfusion injury).
</ul

questions.question: An 11-digit number 8732326687X is divisible by 18. What is the value of X?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by 18 if it is divisible by both 2 and 9.

Divisibility by 2 requires the last digit X to be even (0, 2, 4, 6, 8).

Among the given options (5, 3, 2, 1), only 2 is an even number.

Thus, X must be 2 to satisfy the first condition of divisibility by 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given number: 8732326687X

Condition: Number is divisible by 18.

Method: Check divisibility rules for 2 and 9 (since 18 = 2 × 9).

⇒ Divisibility by 9: Sum of digits must be divisible by 9.

⇒ Sum = 8 + 7 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 6 + 6 + 8 + 7 + X

⇒ Sum = 52 + X

⇒ The nearest multiple of 9 greater than 52 is 54 (9 × 6 = 54).

⇒ 52 + X = 54

⇒ X = 54 − 52 = 2

⇒ Divisibility by 2: The last digit X must be even. Since X = 2 is even, this condition is satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility by 2

A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even, i.e., 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

Composite Divisibility Rule

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, then it is also divisible by their product (a × b).</p

questions.question: A { runs } (5)/(2) { times as fast as } B. { If } A { gives } B { a start of } 80 { meters, how far from } A's { starting point should the winning post be so that } A { and } B { reach it at the same time?}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds A : B = 5 : 2

Ratio of distances A : B = 5 : 2 (since time is constant)

Difference in distance units = 5 − 2 = 3 units

According to question, 3 units = 80 m (head start)

Winning post distance (A's distance) = 5 units = (80 ÷ 3) × 5 = 133¹/₃ m

**∴ The correct answer is 133¹/₃ m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of A = 5/2 × Speed of B

Head start given to B = 80 m

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f448251e41dac07d1e97e068340294ffb6034032120834189dbe25465266ca34.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of A / Speed of B = 5 / 2

⇒ Let the distance of the winning post from A's start be D meters.

⇒ Time taken by A = D ÷ SpeedA

⇒ Time taken by B = (D − 80) ÷ SpeedB

⇒ Since they reach at the same time: D / SpeedA = (D − 80) / SpeedB

⇒ D / (D − 80) = SpeedA / SpeedB = 5 / 2

⇒ 2 × D = 5 × (D − 80)

⇒ 2D = 5D − 400

⇒ 3D = 400

⇒ D = 400 / 3 = 133¹/₃ m

**∴ The correct answer is 133¹/₃ m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Time Property

If two bodies take the same time to cover different distances, the ratio of their distances is equal to the ratio of their speeds: D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂.

Concept of Head Start

In a race of length L, if A gives B a start of x meters, A has to run L meters while B has to run only (L − x) meters.

Dead Heat

A race is said to end in a dead heat if all participants reach the winning post at exactly the same time.</p

questions.question: What is the L.C.M. of 45, 63 and 81?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Factorize the numbers using the largest common factor:

45 = 9 × 5

63 = 9 × 7

81 = 9 × 9

LCM = 9 × (Remaining factors: 5 × 7 × 9)

LCM = 9 × 315 = 2835

**∴ The correct answer is 2835.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 45, 63, and 81.

**Formula Used:** LCM by Prime Factorization Method (Product of highest powers of all prime factors).

⇒ Prime factors of 45 = 3 × 3 × 5 = 3² × 5¹

⇒ Prime factors of 63 = 3 × 3 × 7 = 3² × 7¹

⇒ Prime factors of 81 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 3⁴

⇒ LCM = Highest powers of involved primes (3, 5, 7)

⇒ LCM = 3⁴ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ LCM = 81 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 81 × 35 = 2835

**∴ The correct answer is 2835.**

**__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The HCF is the largest positive integer that divides each of the numbers without a remainder. For 45, 63, and 81, the HCF is 9.

Relationship for Two Numbers

For any two positive integers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. This rule does not directly apply to more than two numbers.

LCM of Fractions

LCM of Fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators). This is essential for simplifying fraction-based arithmetic.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at ₹x and offers a discount of 54% on the marked price. He sells it for ₹437 after charging VAT of 52% on the discounted price. What is the value of x?

x × 0.46 × 1.52 = 437

x = 437 / (0.46 × 1.52)

x = 437 / 0.6992 = 625

**∴ The correct answer is 625.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹x

Discount = 54% | VAT = 52% | Final SP = ₹437

**Formula Used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d809587d8e063f726d363001020707876d55f892bdd2bcf3a08984e0f3ef30aa.png]

⇒ x = 287.5 ÷ 0.46

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the effective change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), while Profit or Loss is calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of two friends, A and B, is 3:4. Four years ago, the ratio of their ages was 7:10. Find their present ages.

questions.question: If the ages of 2 members of a family are in the ratio 6:1, and the average of their ages is 35 years. Find the total of their ages after 11 years.

Total current age of 2 members = Average × Number of members = 35 × 2 = 70 years.

In 11 years, each member's age increases by 11.

Total increase in sum for 2 members = 2 × 11 = 22 years.

Total age after 11 years = Current sum + Total increase = 70 + 22 = 92 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 92 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Ratio of ages = 6:1

Average age = 35 years

Formula used: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

⇒ Age of Member 1 after 11 years = 60 + 11 = 71 years

⇒ Age of Member 2 after 11 years = 10 + 11 = 21 years

⇒ Total age after 11 years = 71 + 21 = 92 years

**∴ The correct answer is 92 years.**

Future Sum of Ages

Ratio and Sum

If the ratio of two quantities is a:b, then their sum can be represented as k(a + b), where k is a constant factor.</p

questions.question: A field is in the shape of a quadrilateral. One of its diagonals is 10 m long. The perpendicular distances from the other two vertices to this diagonal are 12 m and 13 m, respectively. What is the area of the field?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a general quadrilateral = 1/2 × Diagonal × (Sum of perpendiculars)

Diagonal (d) = 10 m, Perpendiculars h₁ = 12 m, h₂ = 13 m

Area = 1/2 × 10 × (12 + 13)

Area = 5 × 25 = 125 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 125 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of diagonal (d) = 10 m

Perpendicular offsets (h₁ and h₂) = 12 m and 13 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of Quadrilateral = Area of Triangle₁ + Area of Triangle₂

Area = (1/2 × base × height₁) + (1/2 × base × height₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/050b4c4960db99d848cc531a779ff71fa9ab903cec3465ce40269204918af517.png] 

⇒ Area = 1/2 × d × (h₁ + h₂)

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 10 × (12 + 13)

⇒ Area = 5 × 25

⇒ Area = 125 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 125 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rhombus

When both diagonals are known, Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂.

Area of Trapezium

Area = 1/2 × (sum of parallel sides) × h, where h is the distance between them.

Area of Parallelogram

Area = base × height. Also, if two adjacent sides a, b and the angle θ between them are given, Area = ab sinθ.

Area of Cyclic Quadrilateral

Area = √[(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)(s−d)], where s is the semi-perimeter (a+b+c+d)/2.</p

questions.question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 8 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 20 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill three-fourth of the same cistern with water?1241

Efficiency of (P + Q) = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 units/hr

Efficiency of Q = (P + Q) − P = 5 − 2 = 3 units/hr

3/4th of capacity = 40 × 3/4 = 30 units

Time taken by Q = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 hours
